question: Consider the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}k&0&0\\0&2k-3&0\\0&0&k\end{bmatrix}.$$ Determine the value of $k$ for which $A$ becomes a scalar matrix, express the resulting matrix in terms of the identity matrix of order $3$, and hence show that subtracting the corresponding scalar multiple of the identity matrix produces the zero matrix.
explanation:
Required Condition

A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are equal. Since the non-diagonal elements of $A$ are already zero, we require $k=2k-3$. Therefore, $k=3$.

Formation of the Resulting Matrix

Substituting $k=3$, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}$$ The identity matrix of order $3$ is $$I_3=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$A=3I_3$$ Thus $A$ is a scalar matrix and also a diagonal matrix.

Verification of the Zero Matrix

Now, $$A-3I_3=\begin{bmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}3&0&0\\0&3&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}=O$$ Therefore, the required value is $k=3$, the resulting matrix is $A=3I_3$, and $A-3I_3$ is the zero matrix.
